name: block-access-map
docs: npx shadcn add @fractera/block-access-map. In a page: { "kind": "block-access-map", "title": "…", "outer": { "title", "text" }, "spaces": [ two to six { "title", "text" } ], "between": "…" }.
use: Who sees what: one frame for the one who sees everything and, inside it, two to six tiles that each see only their own — memory spaces, roles, folders.
avoid: A sequence of steps (use block-flow); a plain list of features with no question of who sees what (use block-cards).
props: { kind: 'block-access-map'; title: string; badge?: string; note?: string; blockKey?: string; outer: { title: string; text: string }; spaces: { title: string; text: string }[]; between?: string }

cases.title: Each element remembers only its own
cases.why: The question is who sees whose memory: the main agent sees every space, each element only its own, and the tiles must not reach each other.

props.title: Whose memory it is
props.note: The deep memory keeps a space for every element.

outer.title: The architect's main agent
outer.text: Sees every space: what each element was told, with the element named.

spaces.title: Mom's element
spaces.text: Only its own: her phrases, files and answers.

spaces.title: Son's element
spaces.text: Only its own: his lessons and questions.

spaces.title: Your site
spaces.text: Only its own: what visitors and you told it.

props.between: Elements do not see each other's spaces.

cases.title: Roles of an app
cases.why: One role sees all records and the others only their own, the same shape as the memory.

props.title: Who sees which orders

outer.title: The owner
outer.text: Sees every order of the shop.

spaces.title: A courier
spaces.text: Only the orders given to them.

props.between: A courier and a customer do not see each other's orders.
